description:
⚠️ **SEQUENCED BEHIND `73-canonical-router-live-transport` (2026-08-12).** The CANONICAL router is the Erlang one, and its `default_transport()` is `fun(_Backend, _Payload) -> {error, <<"no live transport configured">>} end` — `apr_translate.erl`'s own docstring says a backend is *"recognised, reported, never dialed"*, and `translation/crates/wire/Cargo.toml` declares only `serde` + `serde_json`, no HTTP client. So **widening the Rust `wire` codec for a router that cannot dial has no observable effect at run time**: every new rung reaches the same refusal the existing ones do. The work here is still correct and still wanted — it is what makes the router USEFUL once it can dial — but it must land AFTER `73`, or its acceptance criteria can only ever be proven against a transport-less stub and the breadth will read as shipped capability it is not. Do not treat this as a blocker on `73`; it is the consumer.

---

Phase B (provider-router adapter breadth). Widen the Rust `wire` codec (`translation/crates/wire/src/lib.rs`) — OpenAI wire <-> native vendor wire, the CANONICAL Erlang router's hot-path dispatch — past its 8 `(vendor,modality)` pairs it renders today (anthropic/text, gemini/text, replicate/{image,music}, elevenlabs/speech, runway/video, luma/video, minimax/video). Add the pending `(vendor,modality)` pairs in the modalities agora routes each of the 7 native-wire vendors for, so the Erlang router keeps dispatch parity with what the Python/LiteLLM side (51) covers. The codec is a PURE function of the payload (no clock/fs/network; caller supplies `created`) and key order is part of the output (a `Serialize` struct out, `Value` in) — an unsupported pair is an `Err`, never a panic. agora gates on `make check`; the crate gates on `make check-translation` (cargo build + clippy + test), the canonical router on `make check-router-erl` (clean-skips where rebar3 is absent).

userStories.title: Widen the codec's (vendor,modality) coverage with round-trip proofs
userStories.description: Add the pending `(vendor,modality)` pairs to `to_native`/`from_native` in `translation/crates/wire/src/lib.rs` for the modalities agora routes each native-wire vendor for, matching the router's `PAID_PROVIDERS` routing. Each new pair round-trips (OpenAI request -> native body+path -> OpenAI-shaped response envelope) with vendor key order preserved.
acceptanceCriteria: New `(vendor,modality)` pairs are added to both `to_native` and `from_native` so a covered pair renders the vendor's native request (correct path + body in vendor key order) and re-emits the OpenAI envelope for the modality (`chat.completion` / `<modality>.generation`), each with a round-trip cargo test.
An unsupported pair, malformed request, or unreadable response is an `Err` (never a panic, never a partial document); `#![deny(clippy::all)]` clean; `make check-translation` green.

userStories.title: Keep the canonical Erlang router at dispatch parity
userStories.description: Wire the widened codec into the Erlang router's dispatch so the canonical (ADR-0004) router dials every pair the codec now renders — the point of the codec is to remove the `pending-adapter` fall-through for the canonical side, matching the Python/LiteLLM breadth from 51.
acceptanceCriteria: The Erlang provider-router dispatches each newly covered `(vendor,modality)` pair through the widened codec rather than falling through to `pending-adapter`, keeping canonical-router coverage aligned with the Python side.
`make check-router-erl` runs the full gate (compile + dialyzer + eunit + ct) where rebar3 is present and clean-skips otherwise (its host-guarded target); `make check` green.
